subject.title: Feat: Add Trivy SBOM and vulnerability scanning to Docker release

question: After the backfill checkout regression is fixed, should Docker releases immediately fail on fixed CRITICAL Trivy findings, or should Trivy start as advisory-only SBOM/SARIF reporting?
rationale: The PR adds a production release dependency and a release-failing security policy that static checks cannot validate and that may intentionally block Docker releases.

options.title: Fix backfill and require live proof
options.body: Restore current-checkout verification, require redacted live tag/backfill-equivalent workflow output and artifacts, then decide the blocking gate with release/security owner approval.

options.title: Start advisory-only
options.body: Land SBOM, SARIF, and artifact generation but remove the release-failing exit path until maintainers observe successful release runs.

options.title: Accept blocking gate risk
options.body: A release/security owner can intentionally accept the new external scanner dependency and own any Docker release failures after merge.

recommendation.title: Fix backfill and require live proof
recommendation.body: Restore current-checkout verification, require redacted live tag/backfill-equivalent workflow output and artifacts, then decide the blocking gate with release/security owner approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release workflow and release-control history make this the strongest routing signal for the backfill and release-gate decision.
